explain: “At” a time is the ablative: _hōrā prīmā_ = at the first hour. _in hortō_ says where, and _sedent_ agrees with _senātōrēs_ (nominative plural).
distractors: Hōrā prīmā senātōrēs in hortō sedet.
_sedet_ is 3rd person singular (present tense), but the subject _senātōrēs_ is nominative plural: subject and verb must agree. Here you need _sedent_.
Hōrā prīmā cīvēs in hortō sedent.
_cīvēs_ means “citizens”, so this says “At the first hour the citizens sit in the garden”.
Hōrā prīmā senātor in hortō sedent.
_senātor_ is nominative singular, but the verb _sedent_ is 3rd person plural (present tense): subject and verb must agree. Here the subject must be _senātōrēs_.

en: At the third hour the grandmother walks in the shop.
explain: “At” a time is the ablative: _hōrā tertiā_ = at the third hour. _in tabernā_ says where, and _ambulat_ agrees with _avia_ (nominative singular).
distractors: Hōrā tertiā avia in tabernā labōrat.
_labōrat_ means “works”, so this says “At the third hour the grandmother works in the shop”.
Hōrā tertiā avia in tabernā ambulāvit.

_ambulāvit_ is 3rd person singular (perfect tense) of _ambulō_ (“he walked”). That would say “At the third hour the grandmother walked in the shop” instead of “At the third hour the grandmother walks in the shop”.
Hōrā tertiā avia in tabernam ambulat.
_tabernam_ is accusative singular, but after _in_ (“in”) the place goes in the ablative: _tabernā_.
